newsitem.title: GHANA: Cluff Mining to start Ivory Coast operations.
newsitem.headline: Cluff Mining to start Ivory Coast operations.

text.p: Britain's Cluff Mining Plc will start gold exploration in Ivory Coast in April after being granted three permits, according to an Ivorian government minister.

"The new Cluff company is coming to Ivory Coast this month to start their operations," Minister of Mines and Energy Lamine Fadika told Reuters in a weekend interview. "They have three good permits," he added.

Fadika, speaking after a three-day oil and gas conference in Accra which ended on Friday, said Ivory Coast had issued 55 exploration permits, each for up to 1,000 square km, to up to 25 companies over the past two years.
"By the year 2000 we hope to produce five tonnes a year," said Fadika. "Once all the research has been done we hope to move rapidly to 10, 15, 20 tonnes, as in neighbouring countries," he added.
Ivory Coast has two gold mines producing less than three tonnes a year. A third mine is set to open in 1997.
Most exploration firms in Ivory Coast have focused efforts on gold prospection. One is planning a nickel mine.
Ivory Coast shares an underlying gold-bearing Birimian greenstone geology with West Africa's largest gold producer, Ghana, and other expanding gold producers, including Mali.
"A third of Ivory Coast is greenstone, so all geologists agree that the potential is enormous," said Fadika.
Ivory Coast introduced a new mining code in 1996 to encourage investors.
A new Mines Commission was set up on March 31 to streamline management of mining policy and cut red tape.
